cues.zh: 任何时刻，我们都在被感官信息轰炸
cues.en: At any one moment. We are being bombarded by sensory information

cues.zh: 我们的大脑非常出色地把这一切理出头绪
cues.en: Our brains do a remarkable job of making sense of it all

cues.zh: 把听到的声音和看到的景象分开，似乎挺容易
cues.en: It seems easy enough to separate the sounds we hear from the sights we see

cues.en: but there is one illusion that reveals this isn't always the case

cues.en: Have a look at this ah what do you hear ba ba, Ba?

cues.en: But look what happens when we change the picture

cues.en: and yet, the sound hasn't changed in

cues.zh: 每一段你听到的都只是带 b 的 ba
cues.en: Every clip you are only ever hearing ba with a b

cues.zh: 这是一种叫麦格克效应的错觉，Ba，再看一次
cues.en: it's an illusion known as the mcGurk effect Ba take another look

cues.zh: 先专注屏幕右边，现在看屏幕左边
cues.en: Concentrate first on the right of the screen now to the left of the screen

cues.zh: 产生错觉是因为你看到的和你听到的冲突了
cues.en: The illusion occurs because what you are seeing clashes with what you are hearing.

cues.zh: 在错觉中，我们看到的压过了我们听到的，所以嘴部动作
cues.en: In the illusion, what we see overrides what we hear so the mouth movements

cues.zh: 我们看脸时看到的嘴部动作，竟然能影响我们以为自己听到的声音，如果闭上眼睛
cues.en: We see as we look at a face can actually influence what we believe we're hearing if we close our eyes

cues.zh: 我们其实听到的是原本的声音，如果睁开眼睛，我们其实能看到嘴部动作如何影响我们听到的声音
cues.en: We actually hear the sound as it is if we open our eyes. We actually see how the mouth movements can influence what we're hearing

cues.zh: 这是个离奇的效果
cues.en: It's a bizarre effect

cues.zh: 记住，你听到的唯一声音就是带 b 的 ba
cues.en: Remember the only sound you're hearing is ba with a b

cues.zh: 这个错觉的惊人之处在于，即使知道它是怎么来的
cues.en: what's remarkable about this illusion is even knowing how it's done

cues.zh: 似乎也没什么区别
cues.en: Doesn't seem to make a difference

cues.zh: 无论你对这个效应了解多少，它都照样起作用。我研究麦格克效应已经 25 年了。
cues.en: The effect works no matter how much you know about the effect. I've been studying the McGurk Effect for 25 years now.

cues.zh: 我本人就是这些刺激材料里的面孔，这些刺激材料我看过成千上万次，但这个效应依然对我有效。
cues.en: And I've been the face in the stimuli I've seen stimuli thousands of thousands of times, but the effect still works on me.

cues.zh: 我没办法控制。言语脑就是会接收那个信息，它不在乎你带入了什么外部知识。
cues.en: I can't help it. The speech brain just takes in that information, it doesn't care about what outside knowledge you bring to bear.

cues.zh: 麦格克效应告诉我们，我们听到的未必总是真相。
cues.en: The McGurk Effect shows us that what we hear may, not always be the truth.

cues.zh: 但它也帮助我们理解，当感官发生冲突时会发生什么。
cues.en: But it also helps us to understand what happens when our senses conflict.

cues.zh: 当大脑接收到冲突信息时，它会试图理解这种冲突，并且

cues.en: modality is providing more, I guess, salient information, that information might override or at least combine with the other information.
